rv.q: That said, this is largely a joyous show.

Nevertheless, I laughed a lot at this gloriously preposterous and utterly silly evening, and it’s lovely to see the fringe Mischief Theatre, founded in 2008 by graduates of LAMDA as an impro comedy troupe, make it to the West End by dint of sheer hard work and talent.
It would certainly be churlish of me not to concede that I have seldom, if ever, heard louder or more sustained laughter in a theatre.

"The show sits in a fine tradition of British slapstick, and of plays about theatrical blunders... But the trouble is that anyone who has seen, and loved, ‘Noises Off,’ is likely to find the comparison unfavourable: Frayn’s play simply does all the same things, and does them better.
It’s not sophisticated and it’s certainly over-extended; the show’s one-act Fringe origins aren’t hard to spot.
That Goes Wrong will keep going wrong for quite a while. It has a brilliant formula and it earns every laugh.

cn.t: Critics praise this slapstick comedy for its well-executed physical humor and sustained comic premise, though some note the concept of theatrical disaster isn't original, echoing classics like Noises Off.
